column1: depreciate§The equipment depreciates faster than the loan repays, so the company owes more than the machines are worth.§设备**贬值**快过贷款偿还，于是公司欠的钱比机器值的钱还多。§de-（向下）+ preci（价格，同 price 价格）
depreciatory§His depreciatory remarks about her fieldwork were made in a corridor and repeated in three journals.§他对她田野工作的**贬低**之词是在走廊上说的，却被三本期刊转述。§

deprive§The rule deprives part-time staff of the training that full-time staff receive, and both groups do identical work.§这条规定**剥夺**了兼职员工接受全职员工所受培训的机会，而两类人干着完全相同的活。§de-（完全）+ priv（个人的，同 private 私人的）→ 从人手里拿走
derail§One committee objection derailed a bill that had cleared every other stage without a single amendment.§一项已顺利通过其余所有环节、未经任何修正的法案，被一个委员会的反对**搅黄了**。§de-（离开）+ rail（轨道）
derelict§The derelict factory stood empty for nineteen years and is now the most expensive address in the district.§这座**废弃的**工厂空了十九年，如今是全区最贵的地段。§de-（完全）+ relict（遗留，同 relinquish 放弃）
deride§Colleagues derided the method for a decade and now teach it in the introductory course.§同行**嘲笑**这套方法十年，如今把它放进了入门课程。§de-（向下）+ ris（笑，同 ridiculous 荒唐的）

derivative§The score is derivative to the point of embarrassment: four themes lifted almost intact from a film made in 1962.§这部配乐**模仿因袭**到令人尴尬——四段主题几乎原样取自 1962 年的一部电影。§de-（从）+ riv（河流，同 river 河）→ 从源头引出来
derive§The word derives from a term for a hinge, which explains a meaning that otherwise makes no sense at all.§这个词**源自**一个表示铰链的术语，这解释了一个否则完全说不通的义项。§
derogate§Nothing in the agreement derogates from rights the workers already hold under national law.§协议中没有任何内容**减损**工人依国家法律已享有的权利。§de-（离开）+ rog（要求，同 interrogate 审问）→ 部分废除
descend§Fog descended in twenty minutes, and a route the group had walked four times became unrecognizable.§大雾二十分钟内**降下**，一条队伍走过四次的路线变得认不出来。§de-（向下）+ scend（爬，同 ascend 上升）
descriptive§The clause is descriptive, not prescriptive: it records what people already did rather than telling them what to do.§这一条是**描述性的**而非规定性的——它记录人们已有的做法，而非告诉他们该做什么。§
desecration§Villagers called the excavation a desecration, and the dig was suspended before a single trench was opened.§村民称这次发掘是**亵渎**，还没挖开一条探沟工程就中止了。§de-（去掉）+ sacr（神圣，同 sacred 神圣的）
deserter§The deserter was pardoned in 1946 and spent the rest of his life explaining a decision nobody had asked about.§这名**逃兵**于 1946 年获赦，余生都在解释一个没人问起的决定。§
designate§The council designated the marsh a reserve in 1971, and the designation has survived nine attempts to reverse it.§议会于 1971 年将这片沼泽**指定**为保护区，该指定挺过了九次撤销尝试。§de-（完全）+ sign（标记）
desirability§The desirability of the site was obvious to everyone except the geologist, who had read the drilling logs.§这块地的**可取之处**除了读过钻探记录的地质学家，人人都看得出来。§
desolate§The valley looks desolate in photographs and supports nine species that live nowhere else on the continent.§这条河谷在照片里显得**荒凉**，却养活着九个在这块大陆别处没有的物种。§de-（完全）+ sol（孤单，同 solitary 孤独的）
despair§Despair is not what stopped them: they stopped because the funding ran out three weeks before the field season.§让他们停下的不是**绝望**——他们停下是因为经费在野外季前三周用完了。§de-（离开）+ spair ← sper（希望，同 prosper 兴旺）
despise§She despises the phrase "best practice" and has banned it from every document her team produces.§她**鄙视**「最佳实践」这个说法，并禁止它出现在团队产出的任何文件里。§de-（向下）+ spec（看，同 inspect 检查）→ 往下看
despoil§The occupying army despoiled the library, and eleven thousand volumes have never been located since.§占领军**劫掠**了这座图书馆，一万一千册书此后再未找到。§de-（完全）+ spoil（掠夺，同 spoils 战利品）
despondency§Two months of despondency followed the rejection, and the book she wrote afterward is the one people still read.§被拒后是两个月的**沮丧**，而她随后写的那本书才是人们至今仍在读的。§de-（向下）+ pond（重量，同 ponder 沉思）→ 心往下沉
destruction§The destruction was total and the cause was mundane: a space heater left on in an empty room.§**毁坏**是彻底的，起因却平常——一台取暖器留在空房间里没关。§
detachment§She describes her own case with a detachment that unsettles readers more than any amount of feeling would.§她以一种**超然**的口吻讲述自己的病例，这比任何情绪都更让读者不安。§de-（离开）+ tach（钉住，同 attach 附上）
deterrent§The fine works as a deterrent only if it exceeds the profit, and here it is roughly one twentieth of it.§罚款只有超过利润才起**威慑**作用，而这里的罚款大约只有利润的二十分之一。§de-（离开）+ terr（吓，同 terror 恐怖）
detest§He detests meetings that could have been emails and has quietly cancelled eleven of them this quarter.§他**厌恶**本可以用邮件解决的会议，本季度已悄悄取消了十一个。§de-（离开）+ test（作证）→ 当众咒骂着划清界限
detractor§Her loudest detractor became her most reliable citation, quoting her in every paper he wrote for a decade.§她最大声的**诋毁者**成了最可靠的引用来源，十年里他每篇论文都引她。§de-（离开）+ tract（拉，同 attract 吸引）→ 往下拉扯名声
detrimental§The delay was detrimental in a way nobody predicted: the best two candidates accepted offers elsewhere.§这次延误的**有害**之处无人预料到——最好的两位候选人接受了别处的录用。§de-（离开）+ trit（磨损，同 attrition 消耗）
devastate§One bad harvest devastated a county that had spent three generations depending on a single crop.§一次歉收**摧毁**了一个三代人依赖单一作物的郡。§de-（完全）+ vast（空旷，同 vast 广阔的）→ 弄成一片荒芜
devious§The route he took was devious enough that the surveillance team lost him twice in four blocks.§他走的路线**迂回**到监视组在四个街区内两次跟丢。§de-（离开）+ vi（路，同 via 经由）
devoid§The report is devoid of any figure that could be checked, which is presumably why it reads so confidently.§这份报告**毫无**任何可核查的数字，大概正因如此才读着那么自信。§de-（完全）+ void（空）
dexterous§A dexterous technician can rethread the machine in ninety seconds; the rest of us take a quarter of an hour.§**手巧的**技师九十秒就能给机器重新穿线，我们其余人要一刻钟。§dexter（右手）→ 右手灵便
diagnose§Three doctors failed to diagnose the condition because each tested for what his own specialty most often saw.§三位医生都没能**诊断**出这个病，因为各自只检查本专业最常见的东西。§dia-（贯穿）+ gnos（知道，同 know 知道）→ 看透
diagnostic§The diagnostic value of the test is low: it is positive in most healthy people and negative in a third of sick ones.§这项检测的**诊断**价值很低——多数健康人呈阳性，三分之一的病人呈阴性。§
diaphanous§The curtains are diaphanous enough that the room stays bright while the street cannot see in.§这些窗帘**薄透**到房间保持明亮，而街上又看不进来。§dia-（穿过）+ phan（显现，同 phantom 幻影）→ 光能穿过去
diatribe§What began as a book review became a diatribe against the entire discipline and mentioned the book twice.§一篇书评演变成对整个学科的**长篇痛骂**，全文只提了那本书两次。§dia-（贯穿）+ trib（磨，同 attrition 消耗）→ 磨着骂个没完
dichotomy§The dichotomy is false: most cases sit between the two categories, and the interesting ones always do.§这种**二分法**是虚假的——多数情形介于两类之间，有意思的情形永远如此。§dicho（一分为二）+ tom（切，同 atom 原子）

dictator§The dictator kept the constitution intact and simply ignored it, which made him harder to remove than a tyrant who tore it up.§这位**独裁者**原封不动地保留宪法却径直无视它，这让他比撕毁宪法的暴君更难赶走。§dict（说，同 dictate 口述）→ 一句话说了算
diction§Her diction is plain by design: she writes for readers who will not look a single word up.§她的**用词**刻意朴素——她为一个词也不会去查的读者写作。§dict（说，同 dictionary 词典）
dictum§The old dictum that markets self-correct survived four crashes and was quietly dropped after the fifth.§市场会自我修正这句老**格言**熬过了四次崩盘，第五次之后被悄悄放弃。§dict（说）→ 说出来的一句定论
didactic§The novel turns didactic in its final chapter, and every reviewer who liked the first three hundred pages said so.§这部小说在末章变得**说教**，喜欢前三百页的每位评论者都提到了这点。§didask（教）

diffidence§Her diffidence in meetings hid a judgment better than anyone else's in the room, which took the team two years to notice.§她在会上的**羞怯**掩盖了全屋最好的判断力，团队花了两年才发觉。§dif-（分开）+ fid（信任，同 fidelity 忠诚）→ 对自己没信心
diffident§He was too diffident to claim the discovery, and the credit went to the man who wrote it up first.§他**过于缺乏自信**，没去认领这项发现，功劳归了先写成论文的那个人。§
diffuse§The light diffuses through the frosted panel, and the room has no shadows sharp enough to read a clock by.§光线**扩散**着穿过磨砂板，屋里没有清晰到能靠它读钟的影子。§dif-（分开）+ fus（倒，同 confuse 混淆）→ 洒开去
dignify§I will not dignify the accusation with a response, though I have written and deleted four of them.§我不打算回应以**抬举**这项指控，尽管我已经写了又删了四遍。§dign（有价值，同 dignity 尊严）
digress§He digressed for eleven minutes about a train journey and then landed the point so precisely that nobody minded.§他**离题**了十一分钟讲一趟火车旅行，最后把观点落得如此精准，谁也不介意了。§di-（离开）+ gress（走，同 progress 前进）
digression§The digression is the best part of the book, and the author has said she nearly cut it three times.§这段**题外话**是全书最好的部分，作者说她差点删掉它三次。§
dilatory§The department's dilatory response cost the family the appeal window, and the appeal window does not reopen.§这个部门**拖沓的**回应让那家人错过了上诉时限，而上诉时限不会重开。§di-（离开）+ lat（拿，同 relate 关联）→ 一拖再拖
dilettante§He is a serious historian of one century and a dilettante about all the others, and he says so cheerfully.§他是某一个世纪的严肃史家，对其余世纪则是**浅尝辄止的票友**，而且他坦然承认。§
diligence§Diligence alone rebuilt the index: eleven months, one person, and four thousand cards checked by hand.§单靠**勤奋**重建了这套索引——十一个月、一个人、四千张卡片手工核对。§di-（分开）+ lig（选择，同 elect 选举）→ 一件件挑着做
diligent§The most diligent student in the class was also the slowest, and she finished with the highest mark.§班上最**勤奋的**学生也是最慢的，而她拿了最高分。§
diminish§Returns diminish sharply after the fourth hour, and every study of the schedule has said so for thirty years.§第四小时之后回报急剧**递减**，三十年来关于这个排班的每项研究都这么说。§di-（完全）+ minu（小，同 minute 微小的）
diminutive§The diminutive engine produces more torque than machines four times its size, which is why it is still made.§这台**小巧的**发动机输出的扭矩超过体积四倍于它的机器，所以至今仍在生产。§
dire§The warning was dire and the response was procedural: a memo, a meeting, and no change to the schedule.§警告是**严峻的**，回应却是程序性的——一份备忘录、一次会议，日程照旧。§
dirge§The dirge was sung by four voices in a church that could hold six hundred and held eleven.§这首**挽歌**由四个声部唱出，教堂能容六百人，那天来了十一个。§
disaffect§Two years of broken promises disaffected the members who had built the organization in the first place.§两年的食言**离间**了当初创建这个组织的那些成员。§dis-（离开）+ affect（情感）
disarm§Her honesty disarmed a panel that had arrived intending to take the proposal apart line by line.§她的坦诚**卸下了**一个本打算逐行拆解这份提案的评审组的武装。§dis-（去掉）+ arm（武器）
disavow§The party disavowed the pamphlet within a day, and the printer's invoice showed the party had paid for it.§该党一天内就**否认**了这本小册子，而印厂的发票显示是该党付的钱。§dis-（否定）+ avow（承认）
discard§Discard the first reading and the second: the instrument needs eleven minutes to settle, and nobody wrote that down.§**丢弃**第一和第二个读数——仪器需要十一分钟稳定，而没人把这一点写下来。§
discern§It is hard to discern a pattern in eleven cases, and impossible to prove one in fewer.§在十一个病例里**看出**规律很难，少于这个数则不可能证明。§dis-（分开）+ cern（分辨，同 concern 关切）
discernment§Her discernment in hiring is the department's real asset: nine of her eleven appointments still run their own labs.§她在招人上的**眼光**是这个系真正的资产——她任命的十一人中有九位仍主持着自己的实验室。§
discharge§The plant discharged warm water into the river for thirty years, and the fish population changed species entirely.§这座电厂向河里**排放**温水三十年，鱼群的种类完全变了。§dis-（离开）+ charge（装载）→ 卸下
discipline§The discipline is in the boring part: the same measurement, at the same hour, for nine hundred consecutive days.§**自律**体现在枯燥的部分——同样的测量、同样的时辰，连续九百天。§discipl（学习，同 disciple 门徒）
disclaimer§The disclaimer is longer than the advice it qualifies, which tells you what the firm actually expects to happen.§这份**免责声明**比它所限定的建议还长，这就告诉你公司实际预计会发生什么。§
disclose§The company disclosed the breach eleven weeks after discovering it, and the law allows seventy-two hours.§公司在发现漏洞十一周后才**披露**，而法律允许的是七十二小时。§dis-（分开）+ close（关闭）→ 打开
disclosure§Full disclosure would have cost them the contract; partial disclosure cost them the company.§完全**披露**会让他们丢掉合同，部分披露让他们丢掉了公司。§
discomfit§The question discomfited him visibly, and the pause before his answer became the clip everyone shared.§这个问题明显**使他窘迫**，回答前的停顿成了人人转发的片段。§dis-（否定）+ com-（完全）+ fit ← fac（做）→ 打乱阵脚
disconnect§There is a disconnect between what the survey measures and what the department claims it shows.§调查所测量的与部门声称它显示的之间存在**脱节**。§dis-（分开）+ connect（连接）
